messages:
inca (oncall): Incidentbot just fired a Sev2 for routing anomalies affecting capacity tiers. Getting paged now.
incident-bot: [SEV2] SmartRoutingPolicyAlert — elevated fallback rate for hosted->dedicated routing. Threshold breached (5m avg) — auto-page oncall.
inca (oncall): Observed sudden spike in hosted->dedicated spillover for tenant-shard: tenant=acme-inc. Wrong variant landed on dedicated pool. RTTs jumped. Paging diego.
diego: on it. quick check of routing logs now — running `rg "tenant=acme-inc" --stats /var/log/routing/*.log | tail -n 200` to see pattern.
amara: I see churn in model variant mapping around 12:03 UTC. Policy engine tried to fallback region eu-west->us-east and simultaneously applied a tier reassign. Probable race between policy rollout and autoscale.
jackie: Is customer impact confirmed? Maria, can you check open tickets / CS mentions for acme-inc?
maria-cs: acme reporting elevated error rates and 502s for their inference endpoints. CS is on a call with them. I'll post notes.
ops-bot: Temporary mitigation suggestion: add routing override `tenant=acme-inc -> force-hosted` via /policies/overrides (dry-run:false).
diego: Before we flip, need to confirm whether dedicated pool accepts the model variant (quantized vs fp16 mismatch). Logs show "model_variant=redwood-v2-qint8" requested but dedicated pool only has redwood-v2-fp16 registered; fallback created a compatibility shim that failed and retried -> loop.
inca (oncall): That explains repeated fallbacks. Repeating failures triggered more retries and cross-region routing storms.
amara: I'm going to pause the policy rollout that pushed the new tier affinity rules. `PATCH /policy-rollouts/12345 pause` — doing now.
ops-bot: Rollout paused — id=12345 — paused by amara.
diego: Adding temporary override so acme goes to hosted. `POST /policies/overrides` payload: `{"selector":"tenant=acme-inc","target":"pool=hosted-primary","reason":"isolation during incident"}` — applied.
jackie: Confirming with metrics: tailing `routing.events` — after override applied at 12:12 UTC routed hosted hits for acme back to normal within 30s. Drop in retry rate from 48/s -> 2/s.
maria-cs: acme on call confirms errors dropped after ~12:13. They're still on the call asking what caused it.
inca (oncall): Good mitigation. Next: root cause triage steps — did a model variant alias map get updated with wrong compatibility metadata, or did the policy matching rules mistakenly include dedicated pools for hosted-only tenants?
amara: I see a recently merged PR (env:canary) that expanded `tierAffinity` to include `preferredPools: ["dedicated-*"]` for some customers. That PR had a lint pass but skipped integration test for variant compatibility.
diego: Reproducing locally: synthetic request with v2-qint8 to dedicated pool returns kernel mismatch and triggers fallback to region, which then retries to hosted and back -> loop. Patch ready: reject incompatible variant earlier in policy engine and mark as non-fallbackable.
inca (oncall): Action items while we continue: 1) Keep override for acme until fix deploys (jackie). 2) Roll back the tierAffinity PR or apply hotfix to policy engine to check variant registry (amara/diego). 3) CS follow-up and impact summary (maria-cs).
jackie: I updated the override with expiry + annotation: expires=12:45 UTC, note="temporary isolation for incident 1776543210".
amara: Hotfix landed on canary: policy engine now validates variant compatibility against model-catalog before routing decisions and returns a deterministic error rather than triggering fallback. Deploying to prod in 2m.
diego: Rolling the hotfix to prod now: `kubectl -n routing rollout restart deployment/policy-engine` — monitoring.
ops-bot: Deployment event: policy-engine v3.14.2 deployed to prod at 12:19 UTC.
inca (oncall): Post-deploy checks: retry rate stable and no further spillover observed for 10m. Running canary queries across affected tenants.
jackie: Removing temporary override for acme now — we'll keep guardrail in place to auto-reapply if anomalous routing resumes.
maria-cs: I'll send acme timeline + apology + incident number. They want to know what to expect to prevent recurrence.
inca (oncall): Customer impact note: acme-inc experienced increased 502s and latency between 12:03–12:13 UTC. Estimated affected requests ~12k, error budget impact ~0.02% for that tenant. No broad customer outage.
amara: Root cause summary: policy rollout added preferred dedicated pools without variant compatibility gating. This allowed requests for qint8 variant to be routed to pools missing that variant, which triggered fallback loops across regions and capacity tiers.
diego: Fix: 1) Hotfix in policy engine to validate variant compatibility. 2) Add integration test to PR checks that simulates variant/pool mismatches. 3) Revert or tighten the tierAffinity change in next patch.
inca (oncall): Postmortem owners: amara (policy engine), diego (routing infra), jackie (mitigation lead), maria-cs (customer comms). We'll assign due dates and set incident severity to Sev2 -> postmortem within 72h.
incident-bot: Incident 1776543210 updated: status=mitigated, severity=SEV2, assignees=[amara, diego, jackie, maria-cs].
inca (oncall): Closing thread here. If anyone sees any residual anomalies, ping #eng-sre. Thanks all :heart:
summary: Sev2 routing incident — dedicated pool received incompatible model variant causing fallbacks and hosted->dedicated spillover loop; mitigated by pause of rollout, temporary override, and hotfix to policy engine. Customer impact limited to single tenant (acme-inc).
